full_text_en:
Chen Weili v. Lai Guofa — Dispute over Employment Contract

**Plaintiff:** Chen Weili, male, 35 years old, a farmer from Zhongjiang County, Sichuan Province.

**Agent ad litem:** Fan Jun, lawyer of Sichuan Deyang Jinxiu Law Firm.

**Defendant:** Lai Guofa, male, 54 years old, a staff member of Lianshan Town Supply and Marketing Cooperative of Guanghan City, Sichuan Province.

**Agent ad litem:** Jiang Peifeng, wife of Lai Guofa.

**Agent ad litem:** Tang Bin, lawyer of Sichuan Deyang Hongfayuan Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Chen Weili, filed a lawsuit with the Guanghan City People's Court of Sichuan Province due to a dispute over an employment contract with the defendant, Lai Guofa.

**Plaintiff's Allegations:** While employed by the defendant, Lai Guofa, to guard a sand truck, I was thrown from the truck and my left leg was crushed, which was identified as a Grade V disability. I request the court to order the defendant to compensate me for my work-related injuries, including medical expenses of RMB 3,944.20, hospitalization expenses of RMB 2,800, hospitalization living allowance of RMB 900, nursing expenses of RMB 2,000, one-time disability pension of RMB 70,560, one-time disability subsidy of RMB 8,960, one-time medical subsidy of RMB 7,840, wheelchair expenses of RMB 12,800, and attorney fees and travel expenses of RMB 2,000, totaling RMB 111,760.20, and to bear the litigation costs of this case.

**Defendant's Defense:** This case is a labor dispute, which should first be subject to labor arbitration according to law. The injury was caused by the plaintiff's serious violation of operating procedures, and the fault lies with the plaintiff. Moreover, the defendant has already provided timely assistance to the plaintiff, and the parties have reached an agreement on follow-up settlement, whereby the defendant will pay the plaintiff a one-time compensation of RMB 1,000 and shall no longer bear any further liability. After the performance of this agreement, the plaintiff aggravated his injury due to his own reasons, and the defendant should not bear responsibility.

**Facts Found by the Court:**

The plaintiff, Chen Weili, began working for the defendant, Lai Guofa, from August 1996 onwards, primarily following the sand truck operated by Lai Guofa, changing tires, inserting pins into the rotating triangular frame connecting the main truck and trailer when reversing to fix the direction, and reminding the driver to pay attention to safety, among other tasks. The parties orally agreed that Lai Guofa would pay Chen Weili a monthly salary of RMB 300 and provide room and board. On the evening of October 7 of the same year, the sand truck needed to reverse while unloading sand at a location in Chengdu. At that time, the upper and lower pin holes were misaligned, and the pin could only be inserted after the pin holes were aligned while the vehicle was in motion. Chen Weili jumped onto the triangular frame between the main truck and the trailer, preparing to insert the pin while the vehicle was moving. When the main truck reversed, Chen Weili lost his footing on the triangular frame, and his left foot slipped into the triangular frame, where it was crushed by the rotating frame.

The plaintiff, Chen Weili, was admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of West China University of Medical Sciences on the same day for inpatient treatment. During his hospitalization, Chen Weili's father, under financial pressure, reached a settlement agreement with the defendant, Lai Guofa, whereby Lai would bear all expenses of this hospitalization and pay an additional RMB 1,000 for continued treatment costs, with no further liability thereafter. Pursuant to this agreement, Chen Weili was discharged from the hospital on October 21, 1996, with the discharge diagnosis concluding: open fracture of the left tibia, avulsion of the left calf and skin; the patient and his family requested discharge; after discharge, attention should be paid to strengthening nutrition, timely dressing changes, and continued treatment at the local hospital. Lai Guofa paid all medical expenses for this hospitalization.

After returning home, the plaintiff, Chen Weili, continued inpatient treatment at the Zhongjiang County Longtai Central Health Center. He was later discharged due to financial difficulties at home and inability to afford treatment, incurring medical expenses of RMB 2,643.20. After discharge, Chen Weili repeatedly requested the Lianshan Town Legal Service Office of Guanghan City to assist in resolving the matter of compensation for losses from the defendant, Lai Guofa, but to no avail. He subsequently filed this lawsuit with legal assistance provided by the Legal Aid Center of Deyang City, Sichuan Province. On July 23, 1999, the injury of Chen Weili was identified as a Grade V disability through clinical forensic medical examination by the Deyang Intermediate People's Court.

It was also found that on January 13, 1995, the defendant, Lai Guofa, reached an agreement with the Guanghan Lianshan Transport Cooperative, stipulating that Lai Guofa would purchase a vehicle and join the cooperative, operate the vehicle himself, and that the cooperative would be responsible for management and coordination of various relationships and charge certain fees. The vehicle involved in this case (license plate number Chuan F30491) was purchased by Lai Guofa pursuant to this agreement, with the vehicle's driving certificate and other relevant procedures registered under the Guanghan Lianshan Transport Cooperative.

**Opinion of the Court (Guanghan City People's Court):**

The oral agreement reached between the plaintiff, Chen Weili, and the defendant, Lai Guofa, under which Chen Weili provided labor to Lai Guofa and Lai Guofa paid Chen Weili remuneration, constitutes an employment contract. This agreement meets all the requirements for the establishment and validity of a civil juristic act under the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC* and should be protected by law. Pursuant to the Reply of the Supreme People's Court of October 14, 1988, "Concerning the Strict Implementation of Labor Protection Laws and Regulations in Employment Contracts," Chen Weili is entitled to labor protection by law during his period of employment. His injury sustained in the course of work due to his job duties should result in civil liability borne by the employer, Lai Guofa. Lai Guofa has no evidence to prove that the accident was caused by Chen Weili's intentional or gross negligence, and he shall bear full liability for compensation for the accident. The specific compensation standards shall be determined by reference to the *Ministry of Labor's Trial Measures for Work-Related Injury Insurance for Enterprise Employees* and the normative documents of the Sichuan Provincial Labor Department. Pursuant to Article 10 of the *Joint Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Justice on Several Issues Concerning Civil Legal Aid Work*, Lai Guofa shall also bear the necessary expenses incurred by the legal aid personnel in handling the case for Chen Weili. Therefore, Chen Weili's request that Lai Guofa compensate him for economic losses and bear the litigation costs of this case should be supported.

Article 2 of the *Labor Law of the PRC* provides: "This Law applies to enterprises, individual economic organizations (hereinafter collectively referred to as 'employing units') within the territory of the People's Republic of China and the workers who form labor relations with them." The first item of the *Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Labor Law of the PRC* issued by the Ministry of Labor explains: "'Individual economic organizations' in Article 2 of the Labor Law refers to individual industrial and commercial households that generally employ fewer than seven workers." The defendant, Lai Guofa, does not hold an individual industrial and commercial household business license issued by the administrative department for industry and commerce and is not a lawfully established individual industrial and commercial household. Therefore, he cannot be the subject of a labor legal relationship. This case does not involve a labor legal relationship, but rather an employment legal relationship, which falls within the scope of jurisdiction of the People's Court, and labor arbitration is not a necessary prerequisite procedure for this case. Lai Guofa's argument that this case should be a labor legal relationship and therefore should first undergo labor arbitration, and that the People's Court has no jurisdiction, is untenable and is not supported.

After the plaintiff, Chen Weili, was hospitalized for his injury, the settlement agreement reached between his father and the defendant, Lai Guofa, was not the true expression of Chen Weili's own intent and should be invalid. Lai Guofa's defense that, after the termination of the employment relationship, Chen Weili aggravated his injury due to his own reasons lacks supporting evidence and is not accepted. Based on the above, the Guanghan City People's Court rendered judgment as follows:

1. The defendant, Lai Guofa, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, pay the plaintiff, Chen Weili, in one lump sum, medical expenses of RMB 2,643.20, disability pension of RMB 71,442, and medical subsidy of RMB 7,938, totaling RMB 82,023.20.

2. The defendant, Lai Guofa, shall, within 10 days after this judgment takes effect, pay in one lump sum the necessary expenses of RMB 2,000 incurred by the legal aid personnel in assisting the plaintiff, Chen Weili, in handling the case.

3. All other claims of the plaintiff, Chen Weili, are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 50 and other litigation fees of RMB 100 shall be borne by the defendant, Lai Guofa.

Lai Guofa, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Deyang Intermediate People's Court of Sichuan Province, arguing: The appellant is a de facto individual industrial and commercial household and has formed a labor employment relationship with the appellee, which should be governed by labor law. The settlement agreement reached between the appellant and the appellee's father during the appellee's hospitalization, in which the accident handling fee of RMB 1,000 was already received by the appellee's father, who also promised that all future expenses would be borne by the Chen family, has been performed and should be valid. The appellee has no right to file a lawsuit again. The appellant requests the second-instance court to amend the judgment.

The appellee, Chen Weili, submitted to the first-instance judgment.

Upon examination, the Deyang Intermediate People's Court held that: The appellant, Lai Guofa, employed the appellee, Chen Weili, to perform work and paid him remuneration, forming an employment contract relationship. Chen Weili was injured for the benefit of Lai Guofa during his employment, and Lai Guofa should bear civil liability. As Lai Guofa has no evidence to prove that Chen Weili's injury was caused by his intentional or gross negligence, the first-instance judgment holding Lai Guofa fully liable is correct. Since Lai Guofa has not been lawfully registered and approved by the industrial and commercial department, he does not have the legal status of an individual industrial and commercial household and is even less an individual economic organization as defined by law. Lai Guofa's argument on appeal that "this case should be governed by labor law and related laws" is inconsistent with legal provisions and is not supported. Lai Guofa's argument on appeal that "Chen Weili's father has already received the accident handling fee of RMB 1,000 and promised that all future expenses would be borne by the Chen family, so the appellant should not be further liable" is also untenable because Chen Weili is a person with full capacity for civil conduct, and the disposition of his civil rights should be exercised by himself or by a person authorized by him. The first-instance judgment found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, rendered an appropriate decision, and the trial procedures were lawful. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the PRC*, the Deyang Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on March 15, 2000, as follows:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment affirmed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 50 for the second instance and other litigation fees of RMB 100 shall be borne by the appellant, Lai Guofa.
